Jetson Orin Nano — SSD Installation Plan (JetPack 6.0, Native Boot from SSD) Phase 0: Quick Summary of the Approach - Boot from existing microSD running JetPack 5.x (leave it alone, do not flash the SD). - Connect to the internet. - Download JetPack 6.0 final (Jetson Linux 36.2) image. - After flashing, shutdown, remove microSD, and boot natively from the SSD. Detailed Step-by-Step Instructions 1. Boot and Connect - Boot the Jetson normally from your microSD card. - Make sure you have a stable Wi-Fi or Ethernet internet connection. Use `ping google.com` if you want to quickly verify connection. 2. Download the JetPack 6.0 Final Image Get the Jetson Linux 36.2 (JetPack 6.0 final) compressed root filesystem: - Official Link: [Jetson Linux 36.2.0 (JP6.0) download page](https://developer.nvidia.com/embedded/jetson-linux-r362) - Look for the 'Tegra System Profiler', or more specifically, the 'Jetson Linux R36.2 RootFS for SD/SSD installation' type of link. Download the version labeled something like: `Jetson_Linux_R36.2.0_aarch64.tbz2` Save it somewhere easy, like your home directory (`~/`). 3. Install the `nvme-sata-flash` Tool If it’s not already installed on your current microSD system: `sudo apt install nvidia-jetpack` (this usually includes it) If not, we can grab it separately, but JetPack install usually gives it. Careful! Double-check the target disk (`/dev/nvme0n1`) before proceeding. Run: Important flags: - `--storage nvme0n1`: Targets your SSD correctly - `--image`: Points to your downloaded JetPack 6.0 image Double-check the device name (`nvme0n1`) with: `lsblk` Before flashing! 5. Flashing Process - This process will partition, format, and write Jetson Linux onto the SSD. Takes a little while — maybe 10–20 minutes depending on SSD speed. You’ll see status output as it copies and sets up partitions. 6. Shutdown, Remove microSD, and Boot from SSD After the flash: `sudo shutdown now` Then: - Remove the microSD card physically. - Boot Jetson. - It should now boot directly off your new SSD running JetPack 6.0 (Ubuntu 22.04)! You'll get the usual NVIDIA first-time setup wizard (language, keyboard, etc.) — clean system! At this point: - Your microSD remains untouched — you can later plug it into any computer if you left files there. - Your Jetson now runs fully from the SSD. - You have Ubuntu 22.04 with Jetson Linux R36.2 natively — cleanest, fastest setup.
